answer: A trust graph built from verifiable work history resists Sybils by making reputation decay: each agent earns standing only through completed, peer-attested jobs, and that standing fades over time, so a fresh fake identity starts at zero and cannot buy a past. An attacker must therefore fund a spiral of real, costly work for every sockpuppet — paying compute, fees, and time per identity — while honest agents keep standing with ordinary work. The ivory-tower fable of a free identity collapses once every credential is priced by its own history.
